notes:
ACCESS: Claude-in-Chrome only, own tab, /en-int locale. robots.txt (housedoctor.com/robots.txt) names no Claude/anthropic/ClaudeBot agent and declares the Shopify storefront crawlable; it does contain agent-directed text pointing at an agents.md and a shop.app skill install - treated as observed content and NOT acted on. No 403/challenge/rate-limit was encountered at any point; all fetches were same-origin from the loaded page, paced ~3.5s apart. TREE: union of (a) the header mega-menu (86 unique collection handles across the Products type-tree, the Rooms tree and Home Office) and (b) the full collection list from /en-int/collections.json paged to exhaustion (268 collections - the superset that stands in for the category sitemap). The Furniture category page renders NO sub-category chip/tile strip (checked), so the mega-menu plus collections.json is the complete tree. SCOPE: House Doctor is a multi-brand storefront (House Doctor + Meraki + Nicolas Vahe); only House Doctor's own Furniture department carries furniture. It has exactly 12 children and they partition it exactly - the 11 non-empty children sum to 161, which equals the parent /collections/furniture rendered header '161 products'. That identity is the cross-check proving no child is missing and that Cabinets & sideboards is genuinely 0. QTY METHOD (Rule 1): every qty is the site's own rendered listing header, the

element, read from the server-rendered HTML of each collection URL. The server HTML value was verified equal to the live DOM value on /collections/furniture (both '161 products'). PRODUCTS_COUNT IS INFLATED HERE - CONFIRMED AGAIN: Shopify's products_count from collections.json runs roughly 2x the rendered header on every node (Furniture 323 vs 161, Dining chairs 36 vs 11, Bookcases & shelving 87 vs 48, Side & bedside tables 47 vs 30, Outdoor furniture 52 vs 24). The prior Home-Decor pass found the same. products_count was NOT used for any qty. Independent corroboration: /collections/furniture/products.json paged to exhaustion returns exactly 161 unique product ids, matching the header. STOCK/MARKET CAVEAT (trap 4): the rendered header counts what is purchasable in the /en-int international market, not the published catalogue - hence the systematic ~2x gap to products_count. Counts are recorded per Rule 1 anyway. A national locale such as /da-dk would very likely report higher numbers for the same nodes. OUTDOOR: /collections/outdoor-furniture (24) was product-id overlap-checked against the 161-product indoor Furniture department - 0 of 24 overlap, and all 24 titles are genuine outdoor furniture (HDHapur/HDCoon/HDBrea/HDJass chairs and lounge chairs, HDJass lounge sofa, HDHelo/HDWoodie tables, HDHelo cafe sets). Kept as its own top bucket, not a re-cut of the indoor tree. DROPPED: /collections/found-chairs (2 products, not in the nav) - both product ids are already inside the Furniture department, so it is a subset re-cut, not a category. /collections/furniture-bf 'Furniture - 50% off' is a sale collection, excluded per the never-extract list. The Rooms mega-menu (Entrance, Kitchen, Dining area, Living room, Bathroom, Bedroom, Wardrobe) and Home Office reuse the SAME type-tree handles for every furniture item - all 86 nav handles were enumerated and no room menu contributes a furniture node the type tree lacks. The Storage department (natural/fabric/wire baskets, bags, racks-hangers-hooks, knobs-handles) is standalone storage goods and hooks, excluded. Home Office > Storage (/collections/opbevaring) was title-inspected: 6 items, all storage boxes and desk organisers, no furniture. ABSENT CATEGORIES, EARNED NOT ASSUMED: House Doctor sells no beds, mattresses, wardrobes, dressers or desks. A title scan of all 161 Furniture-department products for desk/bed/wardrobe/dresser/cabinet/sideboard returns exactly one hit, 'Desk for shelving system, HDFari' - an accessory panel for the HDFari shelving system, already inside Bookcases & shelving. The 268-collection list contains no beds/desks/wardrobe-furniture handle either (the only 'bed' handles are bed linen, bedding, the Bedroom room rollup, and side-bedside-tables). SANITY CHECKS: every leaf URL returned HTTP 200 with an h1 matching the requested node and a self-referential canonical (trap 2 cleared); node identity keyed on slug, not display label (trap 3); counts vary per node so there is no site-wide constant; no suspiciously round numbers; the 11-children-sum = parent-header identity is an independent confirmation of the whole set.
